grand_strategy.reading:
Iraq in October 2026 is a state whose grand strategy is to be nobody's
battlefield and nobody's client while owning too little force and selling
one product through one closed strait. Its means are access and contracts
(oil for Chinese pipelines, French gas, American majors, Turkish water
works) and its currency is the promise that every patron will be paid
from the same barrels. The Luttwakian pattern is that each safeguard
creates the next exposure: ending the coalition earns sovereignty and
removes the pressure that held the factions; the PMF is state-funded and
so brings foreign strikes on the state; the escape from Hormuz runs
through Turkey, Syria and Kurdistan; the Khor Abdullah claim spent Gulf
goodwill just before the Gulf was needed. The balance with Iran is
structural, not chosen: Iranian gas and the Shia parties tie Baghdad to
Tehran even as the war cut the gas and Iranian drones hit Erbil. Signals
that are not rows: the militias' 'victory' on 30 September is a
statement, not yet an attack; Maliki was stopped by a public American
warning, not by a parliamentary vote; and the date that matters, 30 June
2027, belongs to a government that has filled only part of its cabinet.
Open gaps in this pass: Jordan and Egypt (the triangle), the Gulf grid,
Saudi Arar and the electricity link, Russian arms, the EU, Germany,
water with Iran and the Shatt al-Arab.

stances.note: Transactional, not allied: the 2008 Strategic Framework Agreement is the legal base, the coalition mission ended by agreement on 30 September 2026 (final deal with CENTCOM announced 12 August), and both sides say cooperation moves to economic, development and training fields; al-Zaidi was received by Trump on 13-14 July. Friction is permanent: Washington vetoed Maliki in January, Treasury designated militia commanders on 20 April, the tariff of 24 July, strikes on PMF units that Iraq called a 'heinous crime' (25 March), and US bases were attacked more than 600 times from Iraqi soil. Stable because the withdrawal removes the main irritant but also the leverage. Bond - grievance: the 2003 invasion and the 2020 killing of Soleimani and al-Muhandis on Iraqi soil.

relations_to.summary: Iran works to keep its aligned militias armed inside Iraq: Baghdad's plan to disarm them (PM al-Zaidi: complete by 30 Jun 2027 after a 90-day halt to attacks; the militias ask for end-2027) is met by internal division and Iranian efforts to block it. The groups have struck Kuwait, Jordan, Saudi pipelines and the US embassy in Baghdad.

sources.title: The plan to disarm Iraq's militias: internal division and Iran's efforts to block it

relations_to.summary: Aqaba is the transit port for Iraq-bound cargo - about 37,000 TEU of Iraq-bound transit containers in January-July 2026, up about 930% on the same period of 2025 - but a truck round trip to Iraq takes ten days or more. Aqaba cargo throughput was up about 63% year on year to end-September 2026.

sources.title: Aqaba: Efficiency That Defies Port Pressure

relations_to.summary: Memorandum of understanding of 4 May 2023 for Iraqi crude supplies to Jordan, extended in July 2024 to June 2025, with renewal under discussion in June 2025.

relations_to.summary: In March 2026 Jordan joined the Gulf states in calling on Baghdad to stop militia attacks launched from Iraqi territory (six-state statement of 26 Mar 2026); the Basra-Haditha pipeline is planned to reach Aqaba and Iraq gave the go-ahead in April 2026 for a Basra oil pipeline under a deal with China (mirrored from the IRQ card, same sources).

relations_to.summary: Kuwait holds that the Khor Abdullah median line fixed by UNSC Resolution 833 (1993) and the shoals of Fasht al-Qaid and Fasht al-Aij are Kuwaiti and were never in dispute; it summoned Iraq's chargé on 21 Feb 2026 over the coordinates Iraq filed at the UN in January-February 2026. Iraq says the filing follows international law.

relations_to.summary: Iraq made its final war-reparation payment to Kuwait on 13 Jan 2022, ending a UN Compensation Commission claim of USD 52.4bn arising from the 1990 invasion; the UN declared Iraq to have fully paid.

sources.title: Iraq makes final reparation payment to Kuwait for 1990 invasion
Iraq says paid $50 bln in war reparations to Kuwait

relations_to.summary: Kuwait summoned Iraq's chargé d'affaires on 21 Feb 2026 over maritime coordinates Iraq had lodged at the UN in January-February; Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, Oman, Egypt, Jordan and the GCC Secretary-General backed Kuwait and the GCC asked Iraq to withdraw the filing.

sources.title: Riyadh leads Arab support for Kuwait amid Iraq maritime dispute

relations_to.summary: Iraq's Federal Supreme Court annulled on 4 Sep 2023 the 2013 law ratifying the Khor Abdullah navigation agreement (no two-thirds majority); the president's and the prime minister's appeals were postponed on 22 Apr and 30 Apr 2025 to mid-June 2025 and the outcome is not known to this pass. A GCC-US statement of 20 Sep 2023 called for completing the maritime demarcation.

sources.title: Iraq's top court delays ruling on revoked Khor Abdullah maritime pact with Kuwait
GCC countries, US call for demarcation of Kuwaiti-Iraqi maritime borders

relations_to.summary: Kuwait struck Iran-backed Iraqi militias from its territory in April 2026, according to the Wall Street Journal (Iraqi officials reported at least two rocket attacks from Kuwaiti territory); on 26 Mar six Arab states including Kuwait condemned attacks by Iran and its allied Iraqi armed groups.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait Hit Iran-Backed Militias in Iraq
Six Arab Nations Issue Statement Condemning Attacks by Iran-aligned Iraqi Factions

relations_to.summary: On 17 Nov 2025 Iraq designated Hezbollah a terrorist organisation and retracted it on 4 Dec 2025 after Iran-aligned factions objected; Iran used Iraq for rearming routes (CNN, Telegraph, July 2025).

sources.title: Iraq retracts a terror designation it imposed on Lebanon's Hezbollah and Yemen's Houthis

Iran moves to rearm Houthis and Hezbollah

relations_to.summary: Iran-aligned Iraqi militias attacked Saudi Arabia, shutting the East-West oil pipeline on 10 September 2026 (an Iraqi militant source called it a 'gesture of support' for the Houthis; Trump said Iran was probably responsible); the Houthis have a growing presence in Iraq and train allied militants. The ties are with the militias, not the Iraqi state, which is under US pressure to disarm them.

relations_to.summary: 21 Jan - 12 Feb 2026: at the request of Baghdad the US moves more than 5,700 ISIS detainees from the SDF's former prisons in Hasakah to Iraq (up to 7,000 planned; a US official put the first escapes at about 200 low-level fighters from Shaddadi); the Syrian government takes the Tanf base from the US on 11 Feb. Iraq also sent the PMF's 25th Brigade to the border on 19 Jan. Mirrors the SYR card's row to ISIS (same sources).

sources.title: The decision to move IS prisoners from Syria to Iraq came at the request of Baghdad, officials say
US military transfers 150 Islamic State group detainees from Syria to Iraq
Syrian government and SDF continue transition, US strikes Islamic State and withdraws from Tanf

relations_to.summary: On 29 Jul 2026 Saudi and US aircraft struck Popular Mobilization Forces sites in seven Iraqi provinces after more than 30 drone attacks in 72 hours (the PMF says 20 dead) - the first confirmed Saudi strike in Iraq. The Iraqi national security council condemned it and the prime minister held an emergency session; the GCC backed Riyadh.

sources.title: Iraqi armed groups condemn 'dangerous escalation' after US-Saudi strikes

relations_to.summary: Baghdad and Damascus agreed in November 2025 to commission a technical assessment of the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline (joint committee and international consultant); Iraq already exports limited oil volumes through Baniyas; the Kurdistan Region's president invited al-Sharaa to Baghdad and Erbil on 3 Aug 2026.

relations_to.summary: Prime Minister al-Zaidi's visit to Ankara in late Jul 2026 produced contracts to start the Development Road (energy, transport, education, water), a water 'mechanism document' (signed 2 Nov 2025, ratified by Iraq's parliament on 25 Jul 2026 for implementation from 1 Sep: Turkish firms build water projects financed from Iraqi oil sales) and a one-year extension of the 1973 Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline agreement.

sources.title: Iraqi-Turkish coordination on energy, water corridors as Al-Zaidi visits Ankara
Iraq and Turkey agree to launch Development Road project

relations_to.summary: The 1973 Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline agreement, which carries Iraq's only export route that kept flowing through the Hormuz closure, was extended by one year (agreement reported on 1 Aug 2026 for exports through Ceyhan); the water-for-projects mechanism of 2 Nov 2025 was ratified by Iraq's parliament on 25 Jul 2026.
